profile.headline: Data Scientist II @ Microsoft | Computer Engineer | AI/ML Engineer
profile.summary:
GitHub: https://github.com/dsmith111

I’m currently a Data Scientist at Microsoft Azure. While furthering my knowledge and skillset, I have accrued experience in different areas of engineering, a few of the ones aside from software being in the fields of, industrial, material and mechanical engineering. Through this, I eventually was led to the deeply interesting field of AI. Now I enjoy taking up any chances I get (through my career or even side-projects) to work on AI based systems.

positions.title: Data Scientist II
positions.description:
• Characterized workload patterns for targeted optimization for major customers such as OpenAI.
• Proposed and implemented an agentic data analysis platform used for autonomous storage workload optimization opportunity detection, workload characterization, anti-pattern detection and more.
• Developed a workload simulator allowing for asynchronous experiments and data-driven recommendations for client optimization on Azure Storage. 
• Continued efforts of contributing to open-source libraries such as increasing the compatibility of 
SynapseML's LightGBM model with Apache Spark. 
• Worked with AI and engineering teams across Azure to accelerate ML for efficiency adoption, including assistance in setting up pipelines, managing and training models and handling data.

positions.title: Data Scientist
positions.description:
• Developed the model and supported the corresponding C++ ML library aimed at optimizing memory management with nanosecond constraints.
• Contributed to open-source projects, increasing AI tooling and library compatibility with Windows ARM64 based architectures.
• Developed ML training, validation and deployment infrastructure with Databricks and MLFlow.
• Developed periodic and seasonal based data drift detection tools for increased model reliability based on the KL Divergence derived Population Stability Index.
• Developed custom performance metrics to better represent ordinal label classifiers.
• Reduced engineer workload by automating hyperparameter training and label derivation through the integration of FLAML and the development of a Spark friendly Jenk's Optimization Algorithm.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Costed, designed, proposed and led the implementation of solo and team projects to add new product
 features, increase maintainability or reliability to various Azure services.
• Developed and contributed to open-sourced projects benefiting Azure and Azure customers.
• Mentored and guided interns and new engineers to help them maximize team impact without sacrificing work-life balance.
• Designed and implemented distributed system/micro-services (containerized apps orchestrated with Kubernetes) supporting 99.99% reliability, availability and P99 < 1s latency.
• Fostered organization culture by planning and driving cross-team morale events for hundreds of employees.
• Designed the integration between the Azure Bare-metal cloud service and VMWare, allowing specialized, high I/O servers, designed for Epic Systems workloads to be managed by VMWare and Azure.
• Designed and developed a control plane for the GPU infrastructure used in training/running internal AI models.
• Increased customer satisfaction and trust by providing live site problem investigation and mitigation.

positions.title: AI Consultant
positions.description:
• Designed a latent diffusion tool based on the state-of-the-art Stable Diffusion work at the time that would operate in GPU and non-GPU environments and provide the same features as solutions produced by teams of researchers.
• Implemented these PyTorch diffusion models end-to-end as a scalable docker-based system in a GCP environment through a Flask based API and a Celery based worker/node set up.
• Developed the AI system so that different latent diffusion models/weights could be rolled in with minimal effort.
• Characterized the energy efficiency of multi-node versus vertically scaled AI training methods.

projects.title: End to End Cloud AI Management Infrastructure
projects.description:
https://github.com/dsmith111/quick-cloud-ml-pipeline

Background:
This project aimed to create a quick-to-deploy solution for bringing up the infrastructure and configuration of this infrastructure to handle various stages of AI workflow, from data ingestion and processing to model training, validation, and deployment. That is, anyone should be able to run a few commands to instantly set up an ML pipeline in Azure ready to accept Spark jobs for data management, and distributed PyTorch models for training and serving.

Summary of the Current State:
Pipeline Management: Airflow for handling the triggering of data ingestion and orchestration of the following processes.
Data Processing: Spark jobs to ingest and structure data and store it in Azure Data Lake Gen2.
Model Training/Build: Distributed PyTorch training jobs with results (weights and torchscript) stored in a data lake.
Model Deployment: Automated deployment using Kubeflow Serve for inferencing.
The infrastructure includes three distinct AKS clusters for data processing, training, and serving, ensuring resource isolation and efficient scaling.

projects.title: Cloud Hosted Containerized API Tool for Room Renovation Visualization Backed by Stable Diffusion Models
projects.description:
Background:
This project revolved around the creation of a scalable, cloud-based AI tool, capable of ingesting images of furnished or unfurnished rooms uploaded by potential real estate developers or agents, normalize them (remove all objects), and return a modified version of the room visualized in a chosen style (e.g. minimalistic, rustic, gaming, modern, etc).

The initial version of this tool needed to be able to be used by hundreds of users per day uploading hundreds of images and returning potentially a magnitude more back. All of this also needed to be done within a reasonable timespan.

Summarized Architecture:
The tool was built with Docker consisting of 3 decoupled containers: A Flask front-end/server and API, a Redis message-broker, and a Celery worker-system running on top of a custom Stable Diffusion model and framework. These were hosted within GCP and each division (representing one of the containers) was capable of scaling up and down separately of the others as needed. Servers and workers can operate in a synchronous or asynchronous fashion based on the user's needs.

User Interaction:
A client is given an API key and access to API documentation. With this, they are able to embed the tool within their website, a custom desktop tool, or simply call the API directly through basic commands or Postman. They define a set of parameters within a POST request and send a JSON file along with an encoded image. If they chose to receive an asynchronous response (for more seamless user experiences), they then receive a UID which they can use to build a new URL to query their job's status. Once complete, they'll either be returned a directly streamed image or encoded JSON file based on their preference. The synchronous request works similarly, however, it keeps the initial connection open until the job is finished (better for clients who use no-code websites).

Extra Notes:
The tool was built in such a way that it could be used for topics outside of real-estate.
